Baristas say the powder becomes airborne the second it's scooped. Multiple employees have posted videos describing coughing fits, sore throats, and headaches that only started after the powder was introduced. The union representing 12,000 Starbucks workers publicly called it out: "Breathing in silica powder can be dangerous." The rest of the powder includes maltodextrin, gum arabic, xanthan gum, and undisclosed "natural flavour." None of it is listed on the menu. None of it is disclosed to customers. The powder exists for one reason — to keep your blended drink from separating after it's made. A texture fix. That's it.
